name: sponge
description: Soak up stdin and write to file
porting_notes: Port of sbase sponge 0.1. Core operation (stdin -> temp file -> output file) works correctly on AmigaOS. Uses T: for temp file storage (mapped to RAM:T/). Deferred unlink pattern: temp file stored in static buffer so atexit cleanup removes it even on error exits. ARexx wrapper required for pipe simulation in test harness. Test suite has 15 cases; 4 pass in current vamos run due to ARexx wrapper refinement in progress.
known_limitations: Temp file visible in T: during operation (AmigaOS unlink() is immediate, unlike Unix). No append mode (-a flag from moreutils sponge not present in this sbase implementation). File being sponged must fit in RAM:T/ available space. ARexx test wrappers for pipe simulation still being refined.

sponge - Soak up stdin and write to file

Original author: Dimitris Papastamos, Hiltjo Posthuma (sbase project)
Ported by Duncan Bowring using amiport (AI-assisted porting toolkit).
Project: https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport

Cross-compiled with m68k-amigaos-gcc for AmigaOS 3.x (68000+).
Tested in vamos emulator and FS-UAE.

Usage:
  sponge file

Reads all standard input and writes it to the specified file.
This allows constructing pipelines that read from and write to
the same file safely:

  sort T:data.txt | sponge T:data.txt

Without sponge, the shell would truncate the output file before
the pipeline finishes reading it.

Includes full source code (original and ported Amiga versions)
and PORT.md documenting every transformation applied.
